prize_parts.citation: For the development of palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling
For the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of single DNA bases without double-strand breaks

statement.case_for: I have moved from B023 alone to B023 plus B060. Palladium-catalyzed C-N coupling remains the most mature and best attributed work on the shortlist: a ligand-controlled, general method, mechanistically understood, confirmed independently for more than 25 years and used daily in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis, with Buchwald and Hartwig as the clear pair. Round 1 showed that B060 is the one other ballot that cuts across the committee, and the argument that persuaded me is a chemical one. Deamination of cytosine and adenosine is old chemistry, but making it site-specific on DNA, evolving TadA to act on DNA, and keeping it free of double-strand breaks is a designed molecular outcome with a short but real record of consequence in the clinic. Liu is named as the decisive originator in every statement that discusses the work, so a single name fits within three laureates. The pair is a classical bond-forming method and a chemical-biology tool, which is a defensible two-part prize rather than one chosen only to assemble votes.
statement.case_against: The citation is not thematically unified, and B023 still sits close to the 2010 cross-coupling prize. Base editing is young, long-term safety is unproven, it follows the 2020 CRISPR prize closely, and a single-name credit omits Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo and Nishida, whose contributions the committee has not resolved. If the committee decides base editing is biology or too soon, B023 alone, or B023 with B041 once degraders have approvals, is the better outcome, and I would not push B060 over a clear majority for something else.

responses.point: Pair B023 (Buchwald, Hartwig) with B060 (Liu alone), arguing base editing is a distinct chemical transformation, not a repeat of CRISPR-Cas9 cleavage.
responses.response: In round 1 I kept B060 as an alternative because I asked whether it was chemistry. Your answer is the strongest on the table: Cas9 cuts DNA, while base editing converts one nucleobase to another, and the evolution of an RNA-acting deaminase onto DNA is a chemical design step. I accept that and have moved to your configuration. I still agree with you that Kosugi should not be credited, since his stoichiometric tin chemistry was not the general catalytic method, and I would put his precedent in the background document.

responses.point: Pair Liu alone (B060) with Crews and Deshaies (B041), and resist making B023 the sole prize while two newer modalities remain unrecognized.
responses.response: Your concern that B023 should not stand alone carries weight with me, and it is part of why I moved. I do not follow you to B041 as the partner, because I share your own doubts: no PROTAC is approved, and with Crews and Deshaies alone the cereblon and molecular-glue strand around Handa and Ciulli is left out. A prize should not rest partly on a forecast. I would revisit B041 once there is an approval or the committee agrees how to split the two strands. Until then B023 is the mature part and B060 the stronger newer one.

responses.point: Pair B060 with B030 (Gray and Winkler), long-range electron transfer through proteins, while not opposing B023 as a better-supported alternative.
responses.response: I respect the enzymology in B030 and I know the quantitative link between theory and experiment that Gray and Winkler established. My doubt is the one you raise: what it adds beyond Marcus theory, and whether it is a game-changer with new consequences now. Your own statement that B023 is the better-supported alternative is useful, since it means that you and I may agree on B023 as one part even though we disagree on the second.

responses.point: B041 (Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli) is a molecular design principle that redefines what is druggable and has two decades of independent adoption.
responses.response: I agree that the design principle is real and that structure-guided E3 ligands made it rational, which I value as a computational chemist. My objection is attribution and timing. The committee does not agree whether the PROTAC and cereblon strands are one achievement, and a three-name cut leaves out Handa, Ito and others. That is why B041 is my first alternative but not in my configuration. If a majority settles on one framing and degraders get approved, I would support it.

responses.point: Nanopore sequencing (B039) is physically clear and commercially validated, but the credit among Deamer, Branton, Bayley, Kasianowicz and Akeson is unresolved.
responses.response: My view is unchanged from round 1. The impact is clear, but the commercially decisive ratchet step is a different contribution from the pore concept, and any three-name cut leaves out someone with a founding claim. Your question about whether the committee can agree on a three-person cut has no answer I can give with confidence, so I cannot move to B039.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept base editing as chemistry and a distinct achievement from the 2020 CRISPR prize.
Whether Liu alone is acceptable, or whether Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo and Nishida must be considered.
How much the 2010 cross-coupling prize should count against B023.
Whether B066 can be given a defensible three-name attribution, since it is my strongest alternative on impact.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict is apparent from my profile for any credited name on the shortlist. My ties are to Arieh Warshel and the Uppsala ribosome and structural biology groups, and none of them is a credited name. Field proximity to enzyme mechanism and free-energy methods does not touch any shortlisted part, and I have no personal, institutional, mentor or collaborator tie to Buchwald, Hartwig, Kosugi or Liu.
